clue.text: Nose around church to find a pew

indicators.note: turned around, so the word for nose is read from its last letter back

parts.note: neb is an old word for a beak or nose

explanation.surface: Someone sniffs about a church looking for somewhere to sit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nose' looks like the verb to pry about; it is the old noun neb, and 'around' turns it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A pew is a long wooden seat in church, a kind of bench.

clue.text: Farm building north of main Devon town

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits above, so before, the second

parts.note: a barn is a farm building
staple means main or chief, as in a staple food

explanation.surface: A farm building lies north of the principal town in Devon.
explanation.walkthrough: Devon is a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Barnstaple is a market town in north Devon.

clue.text: Report of no one being religious

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: none means not a single person

explanation.surface: It is said nobody is devout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'religious' is a noun here: a member of a religious order.
explanation.definitionFit: A religious, as a noun, is a monk or nun bound by vows.

clue.text: Seven nymphs being naughty, finally in Hell

indicators.note: one letter is placed in the underworld's name

parts.note: Hades is the Greek underworld

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Seven wicked nymphs end up in Hell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes Y from 'naughty'; 'in' puts it inside HADES.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hyades are the seven nymph daughters of Atlas in Greek myth, also a star cluster.

clue.text: Tom Thumb as a military chap on standby?

definitions.meaning: the tiny folk-tale hero is literally a very small man
an American colonial militiaman ready to fight at a minute's notice

explanation.surface: The tiny fairy-tale hero is pictured as a soldier waiting to be called up.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it describes a tiny person; as one it is the Revolutionary-era militia volunteer.

clue.text: Temporary couturier may

definitions.meaning: stopgap, improvised for the time being
a dressmaker might sew a shift dress, so read as two words

explanation.surface: A fashion designer improvises something stopgap.
explanation.definitionFit: Makeshift means a temporary substitute; split into two words it describes producing a shift dress.

clue.text: The pits in roads terrible? Not so bad!

indicators.note: terrible signals the letters thrown into disorder
not means the following letters are excluded from the mix

explanation.surface: A driver complains about potholed roads, then decides they are not that bad.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange the letters of IN ROADS, then remove S and O ('Not so') from the mix; 'bad' is part of the surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: The nadir is the lowest point, just as 'the pits' means the worst.

clue.text: Article by us

parts.note: the is the definite article
by as in multiplication, three by four, means times

explanation.surface: A piece of writing by ourselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'us' is the newspaper speaking of itself, since the puzzle appeared in it.
explanation.definitionFit: The crossword was printed in this newspaper, so the paper refers to itself as us.

clue.text: Is request excessive? Blokes will admit that it is ill-conceived

indicators.note: admit means let in, so the blokes surround the other pieces

parts.note: men are blokes
beg means request earnestly
OTT stands for over the top

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a demand is too much; the lads agree it's a bad idea.
explanation.definitionFit: Misbegotten means badly planned, or literally born illegitimately.

clue.text: Ecstasy duck gets on river

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece gets on top of the other, so the duck comes first

parts.note: in cricket a duck is a score of nil
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A drug-fuelled duck hops onto the river.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a duck is a batsman's score of zero.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nile is the great river of north-east Africa.

clue.text: Went through case — drank to get drunk

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters reeling into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone empties a case of drink and gets plastered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get drunk' rearranges the letters of CASE and DRANK together.
explanation.definitionFit: To ransack a place is to search through it roughly, often plundering it.

clue.text: Support line that backs freedom

indicators.note: the line stands at the back of, so after, the word for freedom

parts.note: ease is freedom from difficulty or constraint

explanation.surface: A political slogan about a party line that backs liberty.
explanation.definitionFit: An easel is a stand that supports a painting or blackboard.

clue.text: Government department that doesn't permit church doors to stay open?

definitions.text: Government department that doesn't permit church doors to stay open?

parts.words: Government department that doesn't permit church doors to stay open
parts.note: read whimsically, a church service held in secret with its doors shut; really an intelligence agency

explanation.surface: A ministry that insists on locking up the churches.
explanation.definitionFit: The intelligence service of a government is the department whose work is kept secret.

clue.text: Short disease that leads to a premature end

parts.note: curt means brief or abrupt
an ailment is an illness

explanation.surface: A brief illness that leads to an early death.
explanation.definitionFit: A curtailment is a cutting short, bringing something to an early stop.

clue.text: Make similar sounds everyone gets to repeat

parts.note: all means everyone
iterate means to repeat

explanation.surface: Everyone chants the same noises in turn.
explanation.definitionFit: To alliterate is to use words beginning with the same sound.

clue.text: A bygone centre of civilisation with a distinct atmosphere

parts.note: Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia, an early cradle of civilisation

explanation.surface: An ancient city that still has a special feel about it.
explanation.definitionFit: An aura is a distinctive atmosphere or quality surrounding a person or place.

clue.text: Lines oldie disguised with superficial lubrication

indicators.note: the letters are disguised by being put in a different order

explanation.surface: Some old lines of verse are dressed up with a slick finish.
explanation.definitionFit: This flax-seed product is rubbed into wood surfaces, a surface oiling.

clue.text: Support or barrier with chains not breakable

indicators.note: breakable suggests the letters can be broken up and reset

explanation.surface: A post or barrier fitted with chains that will not snap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breakable' rearranges CHAINS NOT; the surface's 'not breakable' misleads.
explanation.definitionFit: A stanchion is an upright post serving as a support or a barrier.

clue.text: Alcohol? After married woman's got it there's nothing left

parts.note: Ann is a woman's name
O resembles zero, nothing

explanation.surface: After the wife gets the drink there is none left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alcohol' is chemical: a sugar alcohol, not a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Mannitol is a sugar alcohol used as a sweetener and in medicine, an alcohol in the chemical sense.

clue.text: Successfully tempt star actor with a second helping of food?

parts.note: the lead is the principal actor in a production
a tray carries a serving of food, as in a hospital meal tray

explanation.surface: A leading actor is won over by a second plateful.
explanation.definitionFit: To lead someone astray is to tempt them into wrongdoing and succeed.

clue.text: Ornamental case showing oriental bird

parts.note: E stands for east, the Orient
the tui is a New Zealand honeyeater, a crossword regular

explanation.surface: A decorated box displaying an exotic Eastern bird.
explanation.definitionFit: An etui is a small decorative case for needles or cosmetics.

clue.text: Multitudes of stars — about a million

indicators.note: about means around, so the stars go round the other piece

parts.note: Aries is a constellation of stars, the Ram
M is the abbreviation for a million

explanation.surface: Countless stars, roughly a million of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Armies can mean vast numbers, as in armies of fans.

clue.text: Possibly finger a fanatical element in society

parts.note: lunatic means wildly extreme or crazed

indicators.note: possibly signals that the word may be rearranged into another

explanation.surface: Someone points the finger at a fanatic in the community.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' rearranges 'finger', and that piece goes last although the clue puts it first; 'a' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the extremist minority section of a group or society.

clue.text: The highest-ranked journalist of all is overindulged

parts.note: top means highest in rank
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: The best editor of all is a glutton.
explanation.definitionFit: To tope is to drink alcohol to excess, so toped means overindulged in drink.

clue.text: Ornament Celts originally buried under hill

indicators.note: in a down clue the letter is placed under, so after, the hill

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

indicators.note: originally takes the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A Celtic treasure found buried beneath a hill.
explanation.definitionFit: A torc is a twisted metal neck ring worn as an ornament by ancient Celts.

clue.text: Open with maiden perhaps at beginning of test

parts.note: in cricket a maiden is an over in which no runs are scored

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A bowler starts a Test match with a maiden over.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is a set of six balls; a maiden is one with no runs scored, so 'perhaps' marks an example. A Test is an international match.
explanation.definitionFit: Overt means done openly and not concealed.

clue.text: Proper pair, a new mum with her first baby?

parts.note: prim means stiffly proper and formal

indicators.note: new suggests the letters remade into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A respectable couple and a new mother with her firstborn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges PAIR and A into IPARA.
explanation.definitionFit: A primipara is a woman giving birth for the first time, the medical term.

clue.text: Greeting that may be part of someone's address

definitions.text: may be part of someone's address
definitions.meaning: abbreviation of avenue in a street address

explanation.surface: A hello that might be found in a postal address.
explanation.definitionFit: Ave is Latin for hail, and also the abbreviation of avenue in addresses.

clue.text: In bed, encouraged to introduce unknown plant

indicators.note: the bed and encouragement words take in a letter between them

parts.note: a cot is a child's bed
led on means coaxed or encouraged
Y is an unknown quantity in algebra

explanation.surface: Someone in bed is urged to bring in an unfamiliar plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to introduce' means the bed-and-encouraged pair take in the unknown, which lands at their join; 'In' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A cotyledon is a seed leaf of a plant, and also a genus of succulent.

clue.text: Volume of music equipment reduced

indicators.note: the word is cut down by losing its final letter

parts.note: a stereo is a sound system for playing music

explanation.surface: Someone turns down the volume on the hi-fi.
explanation.definitionFit: A stere is a unit of volume, one cubic metre, used for timber.
